name: Crigler-Najjar Syndrome Type 2

criteria.description: Persistent unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with serum bilirubin levels typically between 5 and 20 mg/dL
Reduced but detectable UDP-glucuronosyltransferase enzyme activity in liver biopsy or genetic testing
No evidence of hemolysis or liver disease explaining hyperbilirubinemia
Marked reduction of serum bilirubin levels upon phenobarbital therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with reduced UDP-glucuronosyltransferase activity and exclusion of hemolysis or liver disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for mutations in the UGT1A1 gene confirms diagnosis.

laboratory: Normal hemoglobin and absence of hemolysis markers
Reduced but detectable UDP-glucuronosyltransferase enzyme activity
other: Marked bilirubin reduction with phenobarbital challenge test

distinguishingFeatures: High risk of kernicterus in infancy
Intermittent jaundice often triggered by stress or fasting
Normal UDP-glucuronosyltransferase activity or mildly reduced

redFlags: Serum bilirubin levels persistently above 20 mg/dL
Lack of response to phenobarbital treatment
